title: Modeling influence and community in social media data using the digital methods initiative-twitter capture and analysis toolkit (DMI-TCAT) and Gephi
author: Groshek, de Mees, et al.

steps.title: Generate social graph in DMI‑TCAT
steps.instruction: Load the topic of interest into DMI‑TCAT, choose “Social graph by mentions”, launch the analysis, select the top 1500 users (adjustable), then right‑click the result and choose “Save link as” to store the graph file locally.

steps.title: Open graph file in Gephi
steps.instruction: In Gephi, open the downloaded graph file, selecting the appropriate graph type (directed, undirected, or mixed) as required for the dataset.

steps.title: Color nodes by community
steps.instruction: Run Modularity, then open the Partition panel, choose a color palette, and apply it so that nodes are colored according to their community membership.

steps.title: Size nodes by betweenness centrality
steps.instruction: Run Network Diameter, go to Ranking, select Betweenness Centrality, and apply the ranking so node sizes reflect betweenness centrality values.

steps.title: Spatialize graph with OpenOrd
steps.instruction: Run the OpenOrd layout, then run Noverlap (or alternatively run Label Adjust) to prevent node overlap, resulting in a spatialized force‑directed layout.

steps.title: Export visual and statistical results
steps.instruction: After coloring, sizing, and spatializing, export the graph to visual formats (e.g., PNG, PDF) and statistical tables (e.g., CSV) from Gephi for further analysis.
